mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each ultimate beneficial owner's passport (with notarized French or English translation, where applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the UBO's country of nationality / certified translator plus notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Quebec Ministere des Relations internationales et de la Francophonie or Global Affairs Canada) for Hague Convention countries; otherwise consular legalization through the Canadian diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry in the general partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, depending on issuing jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and registered office address for the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal counsel or registered agent of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille (Quebec competent authority) or consular legalization as applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, signing officers, and fiduciaries against the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the Criminal Code of Canada listings, and the Canadian sanctions regulations made under the United Nations Act and Special Economic Measures Act; risk-based PEP verification and enhanced due diligence for PEP relationships; FINTRAC suspicious transaction reporting obligations and prescribed record-keeping under the PCMLTFA apply from the moment of appointment of an agent acting in a business capacity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises – Quebec Enterprise Register portal (https://www.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/en)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name must be in French or have a French version; use of an English-only name is prohibited unless the prescribed exception under the Charter of the French Language is met; the Registraire applies the rules on Roman script, numerals, abbreviations, and phonetic equivalents when accepting transliterated names. All statutory corporate records and registered names must be capable of appearing in French on certificates and declarations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected, the applicant must receive a written refusal notice from the Registraire des entreprises. The applicant may request administrative reconsideration in writing within 30 days of the refusal, stating grounds and submitting an alternate name. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may apply to the Court of Quebec for judicial review within 30 days of the reconsideration decision, or seek a declaration of eligibility under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Extension of a name reservation is generally not permitted; a fresh reservation application and fee are required once the initial 90-day window expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual-only office is not acceptable for a Quebec limited partnership holding a private charitable endowment; a physical registered office in Quebec is statutorily required for service of process and for maintaining books and records. A virtual service address may be acceptable ancillary to a physical office, but the Registraire and Revenu Quebec will treat the physical presence in Quebec as the commercial substance indicator.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236-2245 (Limited Partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), ss. 19-21 and ss. 31-36; Income Tax Act (Canada), s. 248(1) (registered charity definition) for the concurrent charitable grant-making foundation
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), clicSÉQUR Affaires online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Declaration de societe en commandite)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Quebec limited partnership; capital is set by the limited partnership agreement. Contributions may be in cash, property, or services; no escrow account is legally mandated for office-based endowment management activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers hereby create a limited partnership under the Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236 et seq., named [Name] Limited Partnership (Societe en commandite [Name]), to conduct endowment management and charitable grant administration; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the head office shall be situated at [registered office address], Quebec, with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec as the registry of legal publicity; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [General Partner Inc.] is appointed general partner, with unlimited liability, and [Name] is appointed secretary and authorized banking signatory; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the general partner is authorized to file the Declaration of Limited Partnership, pay all statutory fees, and complete all tax, charitable, and occupancy registrations necessary for lawful operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Pre-Filing Compliance Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - clicSÉQUR Affaires online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search in the Quebec Enterprise Register to confirm the proposed limited partnership name is distinctive and not confusingly similar to any existing enterprise. Verify that the name does not contain restricted terms (e.g., 'bank', 'trust company', 'assurance') unless prior authorization is obtained. Prepare the Declaration of Limited Partnership including the name, specific object (endowment management and scientific/philanthropic grant administration), head office address, and identity of every general partner. Ensure compliance with the Charter of the French Language by submitting a French-language version of the name and declaration where required.
required_dossiers: Proposed limited partnership name and statement of object
Name search report issued by the Registaire or an approved search house
Identification documents for each proposed general partner
Quebec-domiciled head office address (lease or notarized letter of consent)
Attestation of authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused on grounds of confusion or contravention, file a revised name request through the clicSÉQUR portal within 15 days at the applicable reduced re-filing fee; alternatively, submit a notarized written consent from the prior registrant or obtain a court order from the Superior Court of Quebec for name homologation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Limited Partnership and Issuance of NEQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Declaration of Limited Partnership electronically via clicSÉQUR Affaires or in paper form to the registration division. Pay the CAD $38.00 (approximately USD 30.00) online filing fee. The declaration must be signed by each general partner or by an attorney-in-fact under a notarized power of attorney. Upon acceptance, the Registrar assigns a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and issues a certificate attesting to the registration of the limited partnership, effective as of the date of filing.
required_dossiers: Executed Declaration of Limited Partnership (original or compliant electronic signature)
Notarized power of attorney if filed through an agent
Proof of head office address (lease agreement or owner's consent letter)
Identification of each general partner (corporate extract or personal ID with Quebec Insurance Number/QIID)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event of a refusal or post-filing query from the Registrar (e.g., missing attestation or defective head office address), file a corrective declaration within 30 days of the notice; clerical errors may be cured by a free correction request, while substantive changes require a new declaration with updated fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Federal/Provincial Business Numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Quebec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for GST/QST accounts with Revenu Quebec and obtain federal program accounts (9-digit BN plus RP, RT, RZ suffixes). Provide the NEQ, the general partner's business identification, and the partnership's mailing address. Because the limited partnership is a pass-through vehicle, the entity itself is not a taxpayer; income and losses are allocated to partners. Confirm the partnership is not required to file a separate income tax return, and ensure each partner is registered for tax where applicable.
required_dossiers: Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) certificate
General partner identification and Canadian address
Bank account details for refund routing and tax deposits
Completed Revenu Quebec registration questionnaire (LM-2/VAT)
Partnership agreement (for tax attribution review)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax account registration is delayed, submit a secure message through Revenu Quebec's online portal requesting expedited processing; in case of misdirected accounts, file an RC155 correction or aggregate remitter adjustment with the CRA to rectify program account linkage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Charitable Foundation Recognition and Grant-Making Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because a limited partnership is not eligible itself for registration as a charitable foundation, the endowment grant-making activities must be conducted by a concurrently constituted registered charity (a trust or non-profit corporation) acting as or associated with the general partner. File a completed T2050 Application to Register a Charity for the foundation entity, attaching the governing trust deed or letters patent, endowment fund agreement, grant disbursement policy, and conflict-of-interest rules. The application must demonstrate exclusively charitable purposes and the disbursement quota framework.
required_dossiers: CRA Form T2050 (Application to Register a Charity) with all schedules
Governing trust deed or letters patent of the foundation entity
Endowment contribution and investment policy
Grant-making and disbursement quota procedure manual
List of directors/trustees with consent to act
Financial statements or projected budget for first fiscal period
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Charities Directorate issues a deficiency or intent-to-refuse letter, respond within the stipulated 60-day cure period; schedule a meeting with the Applications Review Section; file amended governing documents and resubmit the application without the requirement to re-pay filing fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Occupancy, Fire Safety, and Occupational Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality, Regie du batiment du Quebec (RBQ), and CNESST (Quebec health and safety commission)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure an annual municipal occupancy permit for the administrative head office. Verify the premises comply with the Quebec Fire Safety Code and the National Building Code as adopted; register the workplace with the local fire safety service and CNESST. For a pure office endowment-management use, no structural load inspection is imposed; however, the employer must post health and safety signage, file an establishment registration, and maintain an emergency evacuation plan. If HVAC or halocarbon-containing equipment is installed, file the requisite halocarbon declarations with the competent environmental authority.
required_dossiers: Lease or deed demonstrating premises control
Municipal occupancy permit application
Fire safety compliance certificate from the municipal fire service
CNESST employer establishment registration form
Halocarbon equipment inventory and declaration (if applicable)
Evacuation plan and fire drill log
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses the occupancy permit, appeal to the municipal council or the Administrative Housing Tribunal within the statutory delay; for CNESST compliance orders, request reconsideration in writing within 10 days under the Act respecting occupational health and safety, and cure any identified deficiencies prior to re-inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Quebec Minister of Economy, Innovation and Energy (MEIE) and Canada Revenue Agency - Charities Directorate; municipal licensing authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registered Charity Status under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and Municipal Occupational Permit for Endowment Administration; Limited Partnership Legal Publicity Certificate (declaration)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Quebec Minister of the Environment, the Fight against Climate Change, Wildlife and Parks (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category C - administrative office occupancy only; no full environmental impact assessment required provided the site is not contaminated and no industrial process is installed
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge; sanitary discharges must comply with municipal sewer by-law limits (BOD5 equal to or below 300 mg/L, TSS equal to or below 350 mg/L); zero volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from office operations; halocarbon-containing equipment subject to the Regulation respecting halocarbons with maximum annual leak rate of 15%; residual waste managed under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of residual materials.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal fire safety service under the Quebec Fire Safety Code; annual municipal occupancy permit; CNESST workplace health and safety clearance and employer establishment registration; evacuation plan and mandatory fire drill records; no structural load inspection required for low-density office occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online and GST/HST NETFILE; Revenu Québec — online services and CléNEQ; Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Registre des entreprises online registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned limited partnership carrying on activities in Canada and Québec: (i) register the limited partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain a Quebec establishment number; (ii) obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) with GST/HST, payroll, and import/export program accounts through Business Registration Online or Form RC1; (iii) register for QST with Revenu Québec once taxable supplies are made in Québec and the small-supplier threshold is exceeded, unless only exempt supplies are made; (iv) because the partnership is fiscally transparent, the partnership files an information return (T5013) under its BN but does not pay federal income tax on partnership income; each partner reports its allocated share; (v) a non-resident partner carrying on business in Canada may require a Canadian non-resident tax account and should file the appropriate Part I or Part XIII election/return; (vi) if the private charitable foundation is itself a corporation or trust, CRA charitable registration must be obtained separately, and the GST/QST registration of that charity may be administered under its own BN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election; a limited partnership cannot elect to be taxed as a corporation. Available mechanisms include: (i) allocation of income or loss among partners in accordance with the limited partnership agreement, subject to fiscal reasonableness; (ii) voluntary GST/HST registration by a small supplier and voluntary QST registration to claim input tax credits or rebates where available; (iii) an election under the Income Tax Act for a non-resident partner to file a Canadian income tax return on its allocable Canadian-source income; and (iv) application of Canadian hybrid mismatch rules only to deny a deduction or include an amount where a foreign jurisdiction treats the arrangement inconsistently, with no elective override.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax); Québec is not an HST province, so the federal GST and provincial QST apply separately.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold for both GST/HST and QST; registration is mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000, unless the supplies are exempt such as most financial services. A non-resident carrying on business in Canada may be required to register even below the threshold if the CRA or Revenu Québec determines it is carrying on a taxable commercial activity in Canada; voluntary registration is available to recover input tax credits or public service body rebates.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Québec do not impose a mandatory real-time electronic-invoice clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping regime. Suppliers must issue prescribed GST/HST/QST invoices containing supplier name, GST/QST registration number, invoice date, description of supply, and tax amounts. GST/HST and QST returns are filed electronically where required; CRA and Revenu Québec provide optional APIs and authenticated portals, but no per-invoice fiscal clearance or API stamping is mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated at 0% GST/QST when exported from Canada and documentary evidence proves delivery outside Canada. Services may be zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident and not consumed in Canada, or when performed in respect of exported goods. Financial services relating to charitable endowment management are generally exempt rather than zero-rated, unless the supply is an exported supply of a financial service made to a non-resident for use wholly outside Canada; in all cases the supplier must retain contemporaneous contracts, invoices, and payment records establishing the foreign destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CERS electronic export declaration (Canadian Export Reporting System) or CBSA B13A export declaration where applicable.
Commercial invoice and endowment management or grant agreement identifying the non-resident counterparty and foreign destination.
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Canada.
Foreign exchange inward remittance certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank account credit advice evidencing receipt of foreign currency.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny zero-rating, reassess net tax, and impose prescribed interest compounded daily. Gross negligence penalties of 50% of the understated net tax or overclaimed refund can apply. Knowingly filing a false or fraudulent export zero-rating claim is an offence punishable by fines up to CAD 25,000 on summary conviction, and tax evasion penalties may reach 200% of the amount evaded with potential imprisonment. The normal four-year reassessment window is extended where the taxpayer has made a misrepresentation or filed a knowingly false return.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC) as issuer of the Canadian dollar and holder of official international reserves, with OSFI as prudential supervisor for all Schedule I/II banks; the FX control function is largely residual since Canada operates a liberalized IMF Article VIII regime. The Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) licenses and supervises Quebec-chartered banks and credit unions, Global Affairs Canada administers sanctions (Special Economic Measures Act, UN Act-created measures), and FINTRAC enforces the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) across all reporting entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility of CAD on both current and capital accounts; no exchange control, no authorization, and no repatriation approval is required for capital injections, endowment contributions, donations, or outward grant/disbursement flows under the Bank of Canada Act, Currency Act, or any foreign exchange decree. Practical hurdles for this Quebec limited partnership endowment vehicle are: (i) the underlying charitable foundation must hold CRA/Revenu Québec registration and meet the annual disbursement quota (3.5% of non-qualified investment assets); (ii) Income Tax Act s.149.1(6) requires that at least 50% of the charity's directors be Canadian residents; (iii) the LP's flow-through status exposes non-resident partners to Part XIV Canadian tax and treaty-based withholding on taxable Canadian-source income; and (iv) Investment Canada Act thresholds do not affect passive donations but may screen any non-resident acquisition of a controlling interest in the managing general partner. Profit remittance and foreign donor distributions are otherwise unrestricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Nil. Canada imposes no export proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory holding period for export receipts, foreign donations, or investment proceeds. Foreign currency may be retained indefinitely in USD/EUR/GBP accounts without BOC or AMF approval; conversion is a privately negotiated wholesale or retail FX transaction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Multi-currency Operational Account
Fiduciary Custody Escrow / Grant Distribution Operating Account
Capital Escrow Account / USD Clearing Operational Account
Endowment Escrow / Operational plus US Dollar omnibus clearing
Operational Grant Account / US Dollar affiliate (TDBNA) clearing
Treasury Operating and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW as the primary banking rail; MEDIUM as an ancillary FX/payment engine. Canada does not recognize the EU/UK statutory 'EMI' license category. Offshore digital e-money institutions cannot hold charity endowment corpus, issue CAD cheques, accept PCMLTFA-prescribed deposit functions, or open transit/institution-numbered accounts without either a Bank Act (Canada) banking license or FINTRAC money services business (MSB) registration. A Quebec LP with charitable endowment status may use a FINTRAC-registered digital EMI (e.g., Wise Business or Payoneer via a Canadian agent) only for low-value pre-funded operational transfers such as seeding small scientific grants or subscription top-ups, never for the statutory capital escrow or donor-restricted corpus. Legal constraints require full sanctions screening of the EMI's correspondent chain and explicit board-approved treasury limits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical branch visit is NOT statutorily mandated. PCMLTFA and AMF guidance permit remote, non-face-to-face account opening where the bank applies dual-process verification: (i) a verified extract from a Canadian credit bureau or equivalent digital identity source for each authorized director/partner, plus (ii) notarized or apostilled passport copies and the Quebec Registraire des entreprises certificate of status for the LP. Remote opening is therefore permissible in Quebec, but in practice Tier-1 banks require: (a) a live video-call interview with the foundation's executive director and a senior member of the treasury committee, (b) the LP's partnership declaration (declaration de societe) and UBO schedule, and (c) a call-back confirmation to a registered office line. Non-resident partners must in all cases provide notarized ID and, where the bank's EDD policy requires, a banking reference from their country of residence. Direct physical onboarding at a corporate client office in Montreal or Quebec City materially accelerates High-tier approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partner or UBO opacity: >25% ownership held through a foreign trust, foundation, or nominee where the Registraire des entreprises does not publicly disclose underlying owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO schedule naming each natural person; certified trust deed or foundation-governance documents; nominee waiver and attestation; notarized passports; source-of-wealth statement; PEP/sanctions screening waiver for all named parties; written charitable-chain explanation (donor, foundation general partner, LP endowment, beneficiary programs) countersigned by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Status mismatch: entity named a 'private charitable foundation' while the registered charity is expected to be a corporation or trust, and the LP itself cannot hold CRA registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRA Form T2050 (registration application) proof or final charity determination notice; Revenu Quebec charitable-status certificate; LP agreement containing a 'charitable purposes only' special purpose clause; declaration under Civil Code of Quebec arts. 2236-2262 confirming the LP is held for the foundation; letters patent or declaration of trust of the corporate/trustee general partner; registered office and agent appointments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and jurisdiction exposure: proposed beneficiaries or counterparties domiciled in OFAC/SEMA-designated states or on the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Buy-side and grant-side sanctions screening policy with real-time screening commit; attestation of no dealings with listed persons or embassies except as exempt; Global Affairs Canada permitting letter where an exemption is claimed; designated official's signed compliance certification; contractual clause permitting the bank to freeze and hold funds pending statutory guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reputational red flag: charitable-sector abuse (terrorist financing or money laundering typologies) associated with private grantmaking vehicles splitting wires below reporting thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gift acceptance policy and minimum CAD 10,000 EFT/LCTR reporting procedures; audited financial statements of the foundation (latest two years); minutes of the grant disbursement committee; signed confirmation that all donations are recorded in CRA Schedule 7/registered charity information return; no-cash and no-virtual-asset treasury charter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds ambiguity: one-time large donation from a foreign conglomerate or family office into the endowment without commercial invoice.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Donation agreement; source-of-funds evidence (bank wire memo, brokerage statement of liquidation, audited accounts of donor if institutional); charitable official donation receipt template registered with CRA; list of qualified donee status; confirmation that the donation does not trigger Investment Canada Act or Competition Act notification; acknowledgement that no benefit is conferred on the donor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Standard compliant protocol: international wires routed via SWIFT MT103 (with MT202 COV where a cover payment is required) using the entity's own transit/institution numbers; domestic CAD wires settled through Payments Canada Lynx (RTGS same-day finality). Beneficiary line must show the registered legal name of the LP or its foundation general partner and the account number; Field 70 instructions must describe 'DONATION FOR CHARITABLE ENDOWMENT', 'CONTRIBUTION TO CAPITAL' (for GP capital calls) or 'GRANT FUNDING' as applicable. No invoice is required for donations; credits above CAD 10,000 trigger FINTRAC EFT reporting. All foreign-currency wires are converted by the bank's dealing room at agreed-upon rates, with the daily trade-ticket stored in the treasury file. For capital contributions from the foundation general partner, reference the LP agreement capital-account article; for foreign partner capital, ensure treaty-arm's-length taxation memo attached to prevent withholding risk.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Grant distributions and scientific research sponsorship: domestic payments cleared through Lynx (RTGS) for high-value grants, and ACSS for recurring low-value scholarships; US dollar grants cleared through the bank's US clearing affiliate (e.g., BMO Harris, TDBNA) via US Fedwire; international grants settled via SWIFT MT103 with pre-verified final beneficiary information. Where procurement of equipment or services for philanthropic programs is involved, the Tier-1 bank may issue a commercial documentary Letter of Credit (MT700/MT710) or bank guarantee consistent with the endowment's approved investment mandate. The foundation maintains multi-currency (USD, EUR, GBP) sub-accounts to avoid double conversion; all grant funding must match the CRA annual grant list and qualified-donee reporting, with unspent grant balances returned via the same rail to the capital escrow account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable plain-vanilla FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP) with tenors matched to the foundation's quarterly disbursement forecast and an approved bank counterparty list.
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) used solely to bridge temporary currency mismatches between donor inflow and grant outflow, subject to the treasury policy's mark-to-market limit.
Currency options (puts/calls) on a strict hedging-only basis, never speculative, with an independent OTC options confirmation and board-approved maximum premium budget.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic currencies (e.g., CNH, BRL, INR) permitted only where a beneficiary's grant obligation is denominated in a currency with restricted deliverability; requires periodic settlement via the Tier-1 bank and a CRA-compliant prohibited-investment screen.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration (déclaration annuelle) to the Quebec enterprise register, confirming the registered office, general partner(s), limited partnership registration particulars, and business activity of the LP.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Government of Quebec.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the 30th calendar day after the anniversary date of the LP's registration with the REQ.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a C$36.07 (≈US$26.69) additional fee. If the LP remains in default after a formal notice from the registrar, the REQ may administratively strike off (radier) the registration. A struck-off LP loses the capacity to operate as a registered enterprise in Quebec and the limited partners may lose the statutory liability shield for partnership debts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (T5013 and T5013SUM) with T5013 slips reporting each partner's allocation of income, losses, and partnership resource amounts.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally on or before March 31 of the calendar year following the end of the partnership's fiscal period; tax-shelter partnerships are subject to an accelerated filing deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of C$25.00 per day (maximum C$2,500.00) for failure to file the partnership information return; late or incorrect T5013 slips attract penalties of C$100.00 per slip under Income Tax Act subsections 162(7) and 162(8); knowing failure to file may lead to prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RL-15 slips and RL-15 Summary (Sommaire des relevés 15) reporting business income allocations and related amounts to partners who are Quebec residents.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February of the year following the calendar year in which the partnership's fiscal period ends.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties of C$25.00 per day (maximum C$2,500.00) plus prescribed interest under the Act respecting the Administration of Provincial Taxes (CQLR c. A-6.002); deliberate or repeated failure may result in penal prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T3010 Registered Charity Information Return, including financial statements and compensation schedule; required only where the private charitable foundation function is carried by a registered charity (Quebec corporation or trust). A limited partnership is not itself eligible to be registered as a charity under the Income Tax Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the charity's fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Two late filings within any five-year period trigger automatic suspension of registration; if the charity remains in default for six months after suspension, the Minister may revoke registration, causing loss of charitable tax-exempt status and ability to issue donation receipts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No federal or Quebec statute imposes a mandatory independent audit on a limited partnership solely because of its legal form. A compulsory audit is triggered where: (i) the partnership agreement or a funding/grant agreement requires it; (ii) the LP is registered as a tax shelter and prescribed information-reporting conditions apply; or (iii) the philanthropic vehicle is a registered charity exceeding CRA thresholds — gross annual revenue above C$1,000,000 requires audited financial statements, revenue of C$250,000 to C$1,000,000 requires a review engagement, and revenue below C$250,000 permits a compilation engagement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The LP applies Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook — Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). The charitable foundation, if constituted as a corporation or trust, applies Part III — Accounting Standards for Not-for-Profit Organizations (ASNPO). Part I (IFRS) applies only if the entity becomes a reporting issuer under provincial securities law, which is not anticipated for this private endowment LP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LP has no share capital, so no annual shareholder-confirmation or share-transfer filing applies. Annual confirmation of partner structure is embedded in the REQ annual declaration: the general partner(s) and registered office must be confirmed, and under the phased-in Quebec enterprise-transparency regime, ultimate beneficial ownership and control details must be updated when applicable. Transfers or changes in partnership interests are recorded in the LP's internal registers and must be reported to the REQ within 15 days of the change; no separate annual UBO return exists for partnerships under Canadian federal law.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (contributions, distributions, transfers and withdrawals of partnership interests)
Register of General Partner Resolutions and consents
Minute book / partnership records (declaration of limited partnership and all amendments)
Register of statutory filings (REQ, CRA, Revenu Québec)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$110–440 (C$150–600) per year for registered-office and statutory process-agent services in Montreal or Quebec City, excluding notarial transcription and registry amendment fees.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,700–11,100 (C$5,000–15,000) for a full independent audit of a small-to-mid-size endowment LP or related charity; US$1,500–3,700 (C$2,000–5,000) for a review engagement.

stage_6.entry_description: Total value of investment assets, including endowment funds and marketable securities
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foundation receiving foreign contributions, disclose foreign-source grants; foreign property over CAD 100,000 must also be reported on T1135/T1134 as applicable.
